newsitem.title: USA: New Haven, Conn., gets AHL team.
newsitem.headline: New Haven, Conn., gets AHL team.

text.p: A new American Hockey League (AHL) team will play in New Haven starting in autumn 1997, city officials said Monday.
The team does not have a name yet.

The team's players will be supplied by the National Hockey League's (NHL) Carolina Hurricanes, who are working on a joint agreement with the Florida Panthers, New Haven Mayor John DeStefano, Jr., said in a statement.
The 61-year-old AHL is considered the main source of player development for the NHL.
The new team, owned by Paragon Sports Properties, will play a 40-game home schedule at tVeterans Memorial Coliseum.
New Haven will spend $5 million to renovate the 9,000-seat coliseum, DeStefano said.
The city has secured $2.5 million in state bond funds and will spend an additional $500,000 a year beginning in fiscal year 1998 through the year 2002 on coliseum renovations.
Of the $5 million, some $3 million of work will be completed before the start of the regular season in the first week of October.
New Haven has been without a professional hockey team since 1993.
This is the second AHL team to announce plans to come to Connecticut within a week.
The Binghamton Rangers said on June 4 that they will move to Hartford and play next season at the Civic Center.
Connecticut last month lost its only major league sports franchise when the NHL's Hartford Whalers moved to North Carolina.
